changeHome.moveDesc: Copy this harness's hive (every agent, memory, task) and the semantic-memory palace into the new folder. The old folder is left untouched as a backup you can delete later.

resetConfirm.body: This permanently erases all of {{godName}}'s memories and the entire hive, and cannot be undone. Any running sessions will be terminated and the app will relaunch into onboarding. Are you sure?

general.keepAwake: Keep Mac awake while agents run
general.keepAwakeDesc: Blocks display sleep so schedules and terminals keep firing on time. Costs battery, best on AC.
general.simpleModeDesc: Agents brief you in plain language instead of engineering shorthand.
general.desktopNotificationsDesc: Native toasts when an agent finishes or needs your input.
general.autoCompactDesc: Queue /compact for every agent on a schedule (hourly by default; interval in the Triggers tab). Off by default. Long-running agents may overflow their context without it.
general.autoUpdateDesc: Check GitHub releases and download updates in the background; you choose when to restart. Never restarts on its own.

general.dangerDesc: Reset wipes {{godName}}'s memories, the entire hive (every agent, message, task, and the board), the semantic-memory palace, and all settings - then takes you back to onboarding.
general.arabicTerminalDesc: Renders terminals with the browser's text engine so Arabic joins and reads right-to-left (xterm has no bidi of its own). Off is the GPU renderer: faster, but RTL-blind. Applies to open terminals and new ones alike.

persona.headline: AGENTS THAT DON'T CLOCK OUT
persona.body: Atlas runs the CLI agent you already use, several of them at once, long-lived and side by side. It holds everything around them: context, memory, tasks, triggers, files, and integrations. You set the work; they keep going while you're away.

permissions.autonomyHead: HOW MUCH CAN AGENTS DO ON THEIR OWN?

permissions.autoNote: Either way, an agent that goes wrong gets nudged, then limited, then stopped. You can change this for one agent later.
permissions.reliabilityHead: KEEP THINGS RUNNING WHILE YOU'RE AWAY
permissions.reliabilityDescPlain: Agents keep working after you walk away. If the computer sleeps, they carry on when you come back.
permissions.reliabilityDesc: Agents keep working after you walk away. If the Mac goes to sleep they pause, then carry on when you wake it.
permissions.keepAwakeDesc: Stops the Mac sleeping while an agent is running, so timed work happens on time. Uses more battery, so keep it plugged in.
permissions.notificationsDesc: Tells you when an agent needs you. Your Mac will ask permission the first time.
permissions.openAtLoginDesc: Starts Atlas again after a restart, so scheduled work carries on.
permissions.stayAwake: STAY AWAKE ON POWER (YOU SET THIS ONE)
permissions.stayAwakeDescMac: macOS will not let an app change this one. Open Battery, then Options, and turn on "Prevent automatic sleeping when the display is off" while on the power adapter. Without it the Mac really sleeps, and work catches up when you wake it.
permissions.stayAwakeDescWindows: Windows will not let an app change this one. Open Settings, System, Power & battery, then "Screen, blank & sleep", and set the sleep options to Never. Without it the PC really sleeps, and work catches up when you wake it.
permissions.stayAwakeDescLinux: Your desktop will not let an app change this one. Open your Power settings (GNOME Settings, Power, or KDE System Settings, Power Management) and turn off automatic sleep while on power. Without it the machine really sleeps, and work catches up when you wake it.
permissions.askDesc: Agents stop and ask you before they change a file or run a command.
permissions.askDescPlain: Agents check with you before they change anything.
permissions.autoDesc: Agents do the work without asking. This is what lets them run while you sleep.
permissions.autoDescPlain: Agents do the work without asking you first.

triggersTab.intro: The two clocks that act on the floor when you are not at the keyboard: one that hands {{godName}} a recurring prompt, and one that boxes up an agent's context before it fills.
triggersTab.schedulesBlurb: A prompt delivered to an agent on a repeat. Each run is a real turn and costs real tokens, so a schedule earns its place only if you would have asked the same question yourself.
triggersTab.contextBlurb: Summarises an agent's session when it gets too full, between steps rather than mid-task. This is what stops a long-running agent hitting its context limit and losing the thread: leave it on.
triggersTab.webhooksBlurb: Let an outside system post work in.
triggersTab.organisationBlurb: Let a teammate's Atlas message yours.

orgSection.settingsOnly: Settings only, for now. The org messaging service does not exist yet, so a key here starts no connection and nothing is sent or received. It is stored ready for when it does.

contextSection.intro: A rule fires only when both halves agree: the gap since its last run has passed, AND that agent's context is at least as full as the bar. A bar of 0% means the clock alone.
contextSection.compactBlurb: Summarises the context so the thread keeps going.
contextSection.clearBlurb: Discards the context. Nothing is summarised.
contextSection.clearCaution: Clearing throws context away. It is not a smaller version of compaction. An agent mid-task forgets what it was doing. Leave this off unless you keep context another way.
contextSection.extraFocusHint: Appended to the provider's compaction command. Empty sends the bare command.
contextSection.commandHint: Sent literally. Empty sends the bare clear command.
contextSection.contextBarHint: How full the window must be before this may run. 0% = time alone.
contextSection.bigWindowsHint: Used on ~1M-token windows, where a smaller slice is still an enormous amount of text.

memoryPanel.openTitle: Search the shared memory your agents build up
memoryPanel.title: HIVE MEMORY
memoryPanel.intro: What your agents remember across sessions, shared between them. Search it by meaning, not just exact words.
memoryPanel.notInstalled: Meaning-based search is not set up yet.
memoryPanel.plainNotesStill: Agents still keep plain notes without it.
memoryPanel.preparing: Setting up memory. The first run takes about two minutes.
memoryPanel.prepareFailed: Setup failed. Check that Docker is running, then turn memory on again.
memoryPanel.needsDocker: Memory runs in a container on this machine, so there is nothing to install by hand and nothing to download separately. Start Docker, then turn memory on. Atlas builds what it needs the first time, which takes about two minutes.
memoryPanel.dockerStopped: Docker is not running. Start it and memory sets itself up.
memoryPanel.dockerMissing: Needs Docker Desktop. Install it, then turn memory on.

skillsTab.categoryTitle: Categories as published by the catalog
skillsTab.noSkillsInstalled: No skills installed yet. Use add a skill and pick a folder that contains a SKILL.md.
skillsTab.offNote: Off skills are not loaded by any agent.
skillsTab.noneBundled: This build ships no skills of its own.
skillsTab.bundledNote: Ships with Atlas, so everyone who installs it has these. Switch one off and no agent loads it.

workersTab.liveIntro: Short-lived agents {{godName}} starts for a single job. Each gets its own git worktree, so two can work the same repo without colliding; each reports back and is torn down when it finishes. {{godName}} can only start one if you have allowed him to hire, in Settings under Agents & Models.
workersTab.noneRunning: Nobody running right now. Worktrees kept back below are ones whose work has not merged yet.
workersTab.baseBranchTitle: base branch the worktree was cut from
workersTab.preservedIntro: Finished workers whose worktree held un-integrated work. Kept (never auto-discarded) and auto-reclaimed once the work lands in its base branch.

integrations.disabledNoUse: Disabled: no worker can use it.

integrations.testLiveDesc: Runs a live read-only probe against the base URL with the stored secret.
integrations.title: Integrations

integrations.empty: No integrations yet. Connect GitHub or a custom REST API so your agents can use it.
